links.outcome: GPT-4 error detection rate versus radiologists on the same reports
links.effect: GPT-4 detected 82.7% (124/150) of errors, matching average radiologist performance (80.0% to 89.3%; P range .522-.99); one senior radiologist outperformed GPT-4 (94.7%, P=.006).
links.quote: GPT-4 (detection rate, 82.7%;124 of 150; 95% CI: 75.8, 87.9) matched the average detection performance of radiologists independent of their experience (senior radiologists, 89.3% [134 of 150; 95% CI: 83.4, 93.3]; attending physicians, 80.0% [120 of 150; 95% CI: 72.9, 85.6]; residents, 80.0% [120 of 150; 95% CI: 72.9, 85.6]; P value range, .522-.99).

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM as a second-reader quality check to detect errors in radiology reports
Comparing AI versus human reading time and correction cost for report proofreading

screen.reason: Empirical reader study comparing GPT-4's performance at detecting introduced errors in radiology reports to that of radiologists, evaluating diagnostic/detection accuracy and speed rather than a deployment guardrail.
